Subject: Demo request: Dedicated capacity for high-throughput routing (Acme Logistics)

Hi Marissa,

We signed up for a trial on your hosted API yesterday and after a few tests we're interested in a Dedicated deployment for production. A few quick details so you can scope the right demo:

- Workload: real-time route re-ranking + multi-turn chat for drivers
- Expected requests: 150 QPS peak (burst to 300 QPS)
- Typical prompt length: 600 tokens; responses avg ~200 tokens
- Latency target: 90th percentile under 250ms for generation
- Throughput priority: 99% of requests must be under that latency; occasional higher latency ok for long-running ops

I've attached a short doc with sample request traces and a CSV of traffic by hour. We're evaluating Dedicated capacity because we need predictable latency and data isolation. Would love a 30-45 minute technical demo focused on Dedicated sizing, latency tuning (batching/kv cache), and SLAs.

Availability next week (US Eastern): Mon/Tue 10-2pm, Wed after 1pm. If you have an SDR/SE who can run the session that would be perfect - I'll bring our infra lead (Carlos) for the technical bits.

Thanks,
Sara Jensen
Head of ML Platforms
Acme Logistics

Attachment: acme_requirements.pdf (summary + sample traces)

Hi all - Dev here (Solutions Engineering). Thanks for sharing the traces, Sara - useful detail. A couple quick questions to make the demo practical:

1) Model: are you planning to use an open model (e.g., Llama 3-ish family) or a hosted/3rd-party model? Quantization/latency tradeoffs differ by architecture.
2) KV cache behavior: do you expect many repeated prefixes per driver session (we can enable prefix caching to dramatically improve tail latency) or mostly unique prompts?
3) Can you share a sample of max prompt+context size you expect (we saw ~600 tokens avg - what's the 95th percentile)?

I'll prepare a short Dedicated capacity matrix (GPU types, expected sustained QPS, expected 90th/95th latency under different batching and quantization profiles) and attach it. We'll also cover routing/fallbacks and private VPC options on the call.

Pre-read attached: redwood_dedicated_capacity_matrix.xlsx
